## Background

Today we are going to learn all about the **ggplot2** package in R.

There are tons of graphics packages in R.These include "base R graphics" (like the `plot()` function we used last day) and add on packages like **ggplot2**.

### Comparing base graphics with ggplot2

We can use the in-built data frame `cars` to play with plotting:

```{r}
head(cars, 10)
```

```{r}
plot (cars)
```

Now with ggplot:
First, I need to install the package with the `installl.packages()`

>I do not want to run `install.packages("ggplot2")` in my quarto document as this will result in re-installing the package every time I render my report.

Every time I want to use a function from a given package, I need to load it up with a `library()` call:

```{r}
library (ggplot2)
ggplot(cars)
```

Every ggplot needs at least three things: 

- the **data** (data.frame we want to plot from)
- the **aesthetics** (how the columns of the input data map to the plot)
- the **geometry** (how you want the plot drawn, points, lines, etc.)

```{r}
ggplot(data=cars) +
  aes(x=speed, y=dist) +
  geom_point() +
  geom_smooth(method = "lm", color = "purple") +
  theme_classic() +
  labs(x="Speed (MPH)", 
       y="Stopping Distance (ft)",
       title="Speed vs Stop Distance")
```

## Gene Expression Plot

Read the data from online:
```{r}
url <- "https://bioboot.github.io/bimm143_S20/class-material/up_down_expression.txt"
genes <- read.delim(url)
head(genes)
```

```{r}
my_plot <- ggplot(genes) + 
  aes(x=Condition1, y=Condition2, col=State) +
  geom_point() +
  scale_color_manual(values=c("blue", "grey", "red")) +
  labs(x="Control (no drug)", 
       y="Treated (with drug)",
       title="Gene Expression change",
       subtitle = "GLP-1 inhibitor from Novo")
```

```{r}
my_plot + theme_classic()
```

```{r}
my_plot + facet_wrap(~State)
```


```{r}
library(patchwork)
# Setup some example plots 
p1 <- ggplot(mtcars) + geom_point(aes(mpg, disp))
p2 <- ggplot(mtcars) + geom_boxplot(aes(gear, disp, group = gear))
p3 <- ggplot(mtcars) + geom_smooth(aes(disp, qsec))
p4 <- ggplot(mtcars) + geom_bar(aes(carb))

# Use patchwork to combine them here:
(p1 | p2 | p3) /
      p4

(p1 | p2 ) /
  (p3 | p4)

p1 / (p2 | p3 | p4)
```


> How many genes are in this dataset?

```{r}
nrow(genes)
```

>How many are "up" regulated?

```{r}
head(genes)
#genes$State
table(genes$State)
sum(genes$State=="up")
```

> What percentage of genes are "down" regulated?

```{r}
a = sum(genes$State=="down")
b = sum(genes$State=="down") + sum(genes$State!="down") 
round(a/b*100, 2)
```

```{r}
n.total <- nrow(genes)
n.down <- sum(genes$State == "down")
ans <- round(n.down/n.total *100, 2)
```
The percentage of down genes is `r ans`%.




## The GapMinder data

The gapminder dataset is rather famous and has lots of stuff we can plot.

```{r}
# File location online
url <- "https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jennybc/gapminder/master/inst/extdata/gapminder.tsv"

gapminder <- read.delim(url)

head(gapminder)
```

>How many data entries are there in this dataset?

```{r}
nrow(gapminder)
```

>How many countries are in this dataset?

```{r}
length(unique(gapminder$country))
```

```{r}
ggplot(gapminder) +
  aes(x=gdpPercap, y=lifeExp, color=continent, size=pop) +
  geom_point(alpha=0.5) +
  facet_wrap(~continent)
```

```{r}
ggplot(gapminder) +
  aes(lifeExp, fill=continent) +
  geom_histogram() 
```

```{r}
ggplot(gapminder) +
  aes(x=lifeExp, y=continent, fill=continent) +
  geom_boxplot() 
```
